passive-structure-mechanics.summary: Unilateral constraints, taut/slack activation and passive force balance.
passive-structure-mechanics.applicability: Check the frozen current model, task, loads and parameter domain before transfer.
passive-structure-mechanics.limitations: Context only; no current task acceptance, universal stability, global feasibility or hardware claim.
physical_explanation: For ideal fixed payout, g(q)=ell(q)-L<=0, lambda>=0 and lambda*g=0. Slack tendons transmit no compressive reaction. Equilibrium uses grad(U)+Jell.T*lambda-JF.T*F=0 under declared sign conventions.
A compliant length limit permits force-law-dependent extension; it is not automatically ideal complementarity. Pretension, deformation and routing can change the active set.
passive-structure-mechanics.confidence: High conditional on the ideal model; compliant-model transfer must be tested.

general-routing.summary: Route geometry maps tension into generalized force; finite deformation can invalidate local predictions.
general-routing.applicability: Check the frozen current model, task, loads and parameter domain before transfer. Ordinary derivatives require differentiable geometry and a regular fixed active set.
general-routing.limitations: Context only; no current task acceptance, universal stability, global feasibility or hardware claim. Guide contact or switching may break smooth assumptions.
physical_explanation: Virtual work maps tension through the route-length Jacobian. Chord shortening, guide placement and actual solid plates alter length changes during finite bending.

A local row-space match describes infinitesimal kinematics. Finite-load response also requires feasible tension signs, excitation, deformed routes and valid dynamics. Abstract route points are not installed guides.
general-routing.confidence: High for virtual work; route-specific improvement is historical and not universal.

general-equilibrium.summary: Equilibrium, KKT regularity and stability are separate qualifications.
general-equilibrium.applicability: Check the frozen current model, task, loads and parameter domain before transfer. Specify admissible tangent directions and active constraints.
general-equilibrium.limitations: Context only; no current task acceptance, universal stability, global feasibility or hardware claim. Singular tangent systems do not establish physical impossibility.
physical_explanation: Stationarity is only a first-order check. Constraint feasibility, multipliers and admissible tangent curvature are separate; dynamics can leave a locally qualified branch.
On a fixed regular taut set, [Kt,JA.T;JA,0][dq;dlambda]=[JF.T*dF;0]. Kt includes material, geometric and load stiffness. Switching or degeneracy requires branch-aware treatment.
general-equilibrium.confidence: High under stated regularity; global and nonsmooth stability unverified.

general-material-inertia.summary: Material, section, density and inertia change coupled parts of passive response.
general-material-inertia.applicability: Check the frozen current model, task, loads and parameter domain before transfer. Use the actual constitutive law and generator/compiler mapping.
general-material-inertia.limitations: Context only; no current task acceptance, universal stability, global feasibility or hardware claim. Slow simulated decay is not material calibration or proof of a unique relaxation mechanism.
physical_explanation: Constitutive parameters and section geometry determine stiffness; bending uses second moments of area. Density and geometry determine mass and inertia rather than elastic stiffness alone.

Added guides, gaps and section changes can alter stiffness, mass and modes together. Viscosity changes transient dissipation within the declared constitutive model. Gravity and inertial effects must be distinguished from elasticity.
general-material-inertia.confidence: High conditional model relations; hardware/material transfer unverified.

general-multicondition.summary: One passive structure must satisfy every required load under the frozen protocol.
general-multicondition.applicability: Check the frozen current model, task, loads and parameter domain before transfer.
general-multicondition.limitations: Context only; no current task acceptance, universal stability, global feasibility or hardware claim. Tested conditions do not establish untested-load or continuum robustness.
physical_explanation: Loads may select different unilateral active sets or equilibrium branches. Improving one condition can weaken another; combining per-condition designs is not a common-structure witness.
Keep design identity fixed across required conditions and first-use holdouts. Tuning against holdouts changes their status.
general-multicondition.confidence: High as an identity requirement; new-task performance unknown.

general-sensitivity.summary: Mechanism sensitivity and task-performance sensitivity answer different questions.

general-sensitivity.limitations: Context only; no current task acceptance, universal stability, global feasibility or hardware claim. Parameter activity does not imply beneficial task direction or identify multifactor causes.
physical_explanation: Parameter-to-force or stiffness sensitivity establishes model influence (mechanism/M0). Sensitivity of the actual task objective under declared conditions measures task relevance; signs and relevance need not agree.
Valid stable matched ablation can support a tested mechanism. Invalid ablation leaves its effect unresolved; local derivatives cannot certify finite nonlinear improvement.

general-active-inputs.summary: Active force channels, passive length constraints and external loads have different model semantics.
general-active-inputs.applicability: Check the current frozen model, task, load, input channels and time grid before transfer.
general-active-inputs.limitations: Context only; no new Study acceptance, global guarantee, optimality or hardware claim.
general-active-inputs.confidence: Conditional method supported; cross-task and hardware transfer unverified.
physical_explanation: An active tendon tension command is a bounded force input, not a fixed payout constraint. Passive fixed-length constraints cannot silently acquire active control authority.
Distributed/body COM force and rigid-tool mass/inertia have different generalized load mappings. Preserve actual channels, bodies, coordinates, bounds and gravity when comparing models.
After a structural change, inputs can be held fixed for one sensitivity question or reoptimized for achievable performance; declare the treatment and recompute independent task results.

general-task-observables.summary: Holding, timed tracking and directed tool-axis tasks require different observables and time scopes.
general-task-observables.applicability: Check the current frozen model, task, load, input channels and time grid before transfer.
general-task-observables.limitations: Context only; no new Study acceptance, global guarantee, optimality or hardware claim.
general-task-observables.confidence: Conditional method supported; cross-task and hardware transfer unverified.
physical_explanation: Reaching an endpoint does not establish low speed over a holding window or tracking over the time-dependent reference. Match timestamps and required samples.
Tool-axis direction constrains a directed axis, not complete spatial orientation or axial roll. Position success does not establish axis success.
Nominal sampled acceptance is bounded by its frozen grid; between-sample behavior needs separate evidence and cannot be inferred solely from a small sampled margin.

general-finite-claims.summary: Finite success, failure, local rank and tested-count minima have distinct logical strength.
general-finite-claims.applicability: Check the current frozen model, task, load, input channels and time grid before transfer.
general-finite-claims.limitations: Context only; no new Study acceptance, global guarantee, optimality or hardware claim.
general-finite-claims.confidence: Conditional method supported; cross-task and hardware transfer unverified.
physical_explanation: Failure of finite control or structure searches does not prove global infeasibility. A successful tested count does not prove a global minimum; local rank is operating-point dependent.
A strict positive constraint excess remains a failure regardless of size. Internal optimization margins may change without changing the frozen acceptance standard.
Cross-task history can motivate a hypothesis, but task-specific controls and acceptance never transfer automatically. Draft protocol success remains draft success.

validation-active-protocol.summary: Validate active control on exact task identities, observables, sampling and shared structure.
validation-active-protocol.applicability: Check the current frozen model, task, load, input channels and time grid before transfer.

validation-active-protocol.confidence: Conditional method supported; cross-task and hardware transfer unverified.
validation_experience: Reoptimize or explicitly hold inputs fixed after a structural change; preserve candidate/task/control identity. Independent replay owns actual task outcomes.
Retain actual rigid-tool load, external COM forces, input bounds and no-contact qualification where required.
Read all required holding/trajectory/axis predicates over the frozen sampled window. Extra per-timestep diagnostics are additional evidence, not a replacement acceptance standard.
A zero-extra-confirmation selection does not demonstrate repeatability. Formal registered approval, development draft acceptance and bounded custom development checks remain distinct.
